laws.rule: Since 2 February 2026, non-residents pay EUR 2 to enter the inner area around the Trevi Fountain in Rome. Entry is free for Rome residents, under-6s, people with disabilities and a companion, and MIC Card holders. Buy online or at Tourist Info Points; payment at the site is by card only.
laws.heading: Roma Capitale, Fontana di Trevi ticket

laws.rule: Rome's Police Regulation (Regolamento di Polizia Urbana, 2019) bans bathing in the city's historic fountains, and also misusing them: throwing objects or liquids in, putting animals in, climbing on them or lying on them. The fountains named are the Trevi Fountain, the Fontana dei Leoni in Piazza del Popolo, the Barcaccia in Piazza di Spagna and the Fontanone on the Janiculum; others are in an annex. Tossing coins into the Trevi Fountain is expressly allowed. The reduced fine for bathing in a historic fountain or misusing a fountain or drinking-water tap (nasone) ranges from EUR 160 to EUR 450 depending on severity (about A$254 to A$715 at the RBA rate of 30 October 2026, A$1 = EUR 0.6293); the regulation also allows a 48-hour order barring a person from certain city areas. Figures are the city's 2019 notices; the city's regulations list shows later amendments that were not read.
laws.penalty_signal: EUR 160 to EUR 450 reduced fine (about A$254 to A$715); 48-hour area ban
laws.heading: Roma Capitale, Regolamento di Polizia Urbana (Assemblea Capitolina 2019; fines table by Giunta Capitolina 5 July 2019)

laws.rule: Under the same regulation: shops, takeaways and vending machines may not sell alcohol from 10 pm to 7 am; drinking from glass containers on public streets and unfenced green areas is banned from 10 pm to 7 am; drinking any alcohol from any container there is banned from 11 pm to 7 am; and bars and clubs may not serve alcohol from 3 am to 7 am. Organising or promoting routes aimed only at drinking between pubs and bars (pub crawls) is banned. The mayor can set further limits by ordinance. Fines for the alcohol rules range from EUR 160 to EUR 400 (about A$254 to A$636). These are the 2019 notices; later amendments were not read.
laws.penalty_signal: EUR 160 to EUR 400 (about A$254 to A$636)
laws.heading: Roma Capitale, Regolamento di Polizia Urbana (2019)

laws.rule: Under the same regulation, graffiti, defacing or damaging historic, artistic or monumental assets and places of worship carries a minimum reduced fine of EUR 400 (about A$636), and the damage must be restored. Sleeping or camping in public spaces (bivacchi) and unauthorised street selling are fined from EUR 250 to EUR 400 for the more serious cases (about A$397 to A$636).
laws.penalty_signal: from EUR 400 for damaging monuments (about A$636)

sites.name: Etruscan Necropolises of Cerveteri (Banditaccia) and Tarquinia (Monterozzi)
sites.what: Two Etruscan cemeteries north of Rome: Cerveteri's tumulus tombs and Tarquinia's painted tombs (UNESCO World Heritage).

access.opening: Tuesday to Sunday, closed Mondays. 25 October 2026 to 27 March 2027: 9 am to 5 pm, last entry 4 pm; from 29 March to 12 October 2026 the park listed 9 am to 7.30 pm.
access.tickets: One city's museum and necropolis EUR 13 (about AUD 21, RBA rate 30 October 2026), valid 30 days; all four park sites EUR 21 (about AUD 33, RBA rate 30 October 2026), valid four months. Under 18s free; EU citizens aged 18 to 25 pay EUR 2. Free on the Ministry's free Sundays.
access.closures: The Banditaccia and Monterozzi areas may close on weather-alert days; the park advises phoning 06 9940001 (Banditaccia) or 0766 856308 (Monterozzi) first.
